options.text: A web-based graphical interface for managing Azure resources

explanation: The portal is the browser-based GUI for Azure.

why_wrong.a: Command-line tools include Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell.
why_wrong.d: Templates are ARM templates and Bicep files.
why_wrong.c: Billing is handled by Cost Management and Billing.

options.text: A browser-based shell with Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell already installed and signed in
A physical device shipped to your office
A virtual machine you must build yourself

explanation: Cloud Shell gives you a ready-to-use command line in the browser.

why_wrong.b: Cloud Shell is a service, not hardware.
why_wrong.c: You do not build anything to use it.

prompt: Which statement about Azure CLI is true?

options.text: It runs only inside the Azure portal
It is cross-platform and runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
It is only a graphical tool

explanation: Azure CLI is a cross-platform command-line tool.

why_wrong.a: It also runs on your own computer and in Cloud Shell.
why_wrong.d: It runs on several operating systems.

prompt: Which command creates a resource group using Azure CLI?
explanation: Azure CLI commands start with az.

why_wrong.b: That is the Azure PowerShell cmdlet.

prompt: What is the purpose of Azure Arc?

options.text: To extend Azure management to resources outside Azure, such as on-premises servers and other clouds

explanation: Arc projects outside resources into Azure so they can be managed with Azure tools.

why_wrong.b: Costs are estimated with the pricing calculator.

prompt: A company has servers on-premises and in another cloud and wants to apply Azure Policy and tags to them. What should it use?
explanation: Arc brings those servers under Azure management.

options.text: Managing and provisioning infrastructure with definition files instead of manual steps
Clicking through the portal for each deployment

explanation: IaC defines infrastructure in files that can be versioned and reused.

why_wrong.c: Manual clicking is what IaC replaces.

prompt: Which is a benefit of infrastructure as code?

options.text: It removes the need for Azure
It requires manual steps for every deployment

explanation: Definition files make deployments repeatable and consistent.

why_wrong.d: IaC does not guarantee a price.
why_wrong.a: IaC is used to deploy to Azure.

prompt: Requests from the Azure portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell and REST APIs are all processed by which service?
explanation: ARM is the management layer that every tool talks to.

prompt: Which TWO statements about ARM templates are true? (Select two.)

options.text: They can be reused to deploy the same environment repeatedly
They can only deploy virtual machines
They must be created by clicking in the portal each time
They describe the desired end state (declarative)

explanation: ARM templates are declarative and reusable.

why_wrong.b: They can deploy many resource types.
why_wrong.c: They are files you can write and reuse.
why_wrong.d: ARM deploys the templates; they do not replace it.

prompt: Which TWO are command-line tools for managing Azure? (Select two.)
explanation: Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell are command-line tools.

why_wrong.d: Service Health reports on service issues.

prompt: Decide whether each statement is true.

options.text: Azure Cloud Shell can run Azure CLI or Azure PowerShell in a browser.
Bicep files compile to ARM templates.
Azure Arc can only manage resources inside Azure.

explanation: Cloud Shell runs both tools and Bicep compiles to ARM; Arc exists to manage resources outside Azure.

why_wrong.s2: Yes. Bicep is a shorter language that compiles to ARM templates.
why_wrong.s3: No. Arc extends management to resources outside Azure.
